entry.title: TakeCar: a Syrian app for ride sharing between cities, city rides and delivery
entry.summary: TakeCar is the Syrian mobility app our team builds at Alhamou. Drivers fill the empty seats on trips they already make, passengers travel between governorates for less, and the same app covers rides inside the city and delivery.
entry.content:
What is TakeCar?

TakeCar (تيك كار in Arabic) is a mobility app built for Syria. It brings riders and drivers together in one simple experience. Shared rides between governorates are at the heart of the app, and the same app also covers rides inside the city and delivery.

Our team at Alhamou builds TakeCar, and it is our flagship project. We design it for the Syrian market, with a focus on flexibility, ease of use and technology that is owned locally.

How shared rides work

Many drivers travel between Syrian cities anyway, and they often leave with empty seats. With TakeCar, a driver sells the seats of a trip they have already planned at a reduced price instead of travelling empty. Passengers get a shared ride they can rely on, at a good price.

Both sides gain. The driver earns from seats that would have stayed empty, and the passenger travels between governorates for less.

More than intercity trips

TakeCar is not only for long trips. The same app covers rides inside the city and delivery, so one app serves the different ways people and parcels move around.

Built for the Syrian market

  • One experience for riders and drivers: both sides use the same simple app.
  • Flexible pricing and live offers: prices stay flexible, and offers are made live.
  • Maps and routing tuned for the local market: directions that fit the roads and places where the app is used.
  • Infrastructure built to scale: a technical base made to grow with the number of riders and drivers.

Who is behind TakeCar

We are a team of developers at Alhamou, and we build TakeCar together. We follow the same rule in everything we make: good technology does not show off its complexity, it makes people's lives simpler.

Frequently asked questions

What is TakeCar?

TakeCar is a Syrian app for ride sharing and transport. Drivers sell the empty seats of trips they already plan, passengers travel between governorates for less, and the app also covers city rides and delivery.

How does TakeCar make travel cheaper?

A driver who is making a trip anyway sells the empty seats at a reduced price instead of travelling empty. Passengers share the ride, so each of them pays for a seat rather than for a whole car.

Does TakeCar also offer city rides and delivery?

Yes. Besides shared trips between governorates, TakeCar covers rides inside the city and delivery.

Where does TakeCar work?

TakeCar is built for Syria, for trips between governorates and rides inside cities.

Who builds TakeCar?

TakeCar is built by Alhamou, a team of developers, as its flagship project.

Where can I get TakeCar?

Start at takecarapp.com, the official website of the app.

entry.title: Nadhif: clean your Mac with developer tools and protect your website and server from hackers
entry.summary: Nadhif is the Mac app our team is building at Alhamou. It cleans your Mac and explains every file before it touches it, gives developers tools for the gigabytes Xcode, Node and Docker leave behind, and tests your websites and servers for vulnerabilities, so you can close them before anyone uses them.
entry.content:
What is Nadhif?

Nadhif (Arabic for “clean”) is a native macOS app for Macs with Apple silicon running macOS 15 or later. It does three jobs in one quiet window: it cleans your Mac without risk, it clears the space your developer tools quietly fill, and it finds the weak spots in your Mac, your servers and your websites before hackers do.

Our team at Alhamou has been building Nadhif since September 2026, and it is still in active development. The app speaks English, German and Arabic.

Clean your Mac without the fear

Most cleaners ask you to trust one big button. Nadhif works the other way round. A single scan finds caches, logs, developer leftovers, old installers and large files, and every category comes with one line that explains what it is and why removing it is safe, or why it is not. You decide what goes.

Cleaning is a move, not a delete. Everything Nadhif cleans goes to Recently Cleaned, where you can restore it for seven days. Your personal files and your keys are off limits.

The uninstaller removes an app together with its files in Library, and finds what is left of apps you deleted before.

Tools for developers

A developer's Mac fills up in places most cleaners never look. Nadhif knows them: Xcode data, simulators, node_modules folders, Homebrew and Docker, the places that quietly eat gigabytes on a developer's Mac.

Protect your website and server from hackers

The third part of Nadhif looks for the gaps attackers get in through:

  • This Mac: a security check of the Mac you are working on.
  • Servers: scans Debian and Ubuntu servers for vulnerabilities over SSH.
  • Websites: tests the websites you own with real attack techniques, so you find weak spots before someone else does.

Private by design

Nadhif collects no personal data and leaves no process running in the background. Scan results and security reports stay on your Mac.

Who is behind Nadhif

We are a team of developers at Alhamou, and we build Nadhif together. We follow the same rule in everything we make: good technology does not show off its complexity, it makes people's lives simpler.

Frequently asked questions

Is Nadhif safe to use?

Yes. Nadhif explains every category before it cleans, never touches your personal files or keys, and moves everything it cleans to Recently Cleaned for seven days, so you can undo any cleanup.

What do I need to run Nadhif?

A Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later.

Does Nadhif collect my data?

No. Nadhif collects no personal data, and its reports stay on your Mac.

Does Nadhif have tools for developers?

Yes. Nadhif finds and cleans what Xcode, simulators, node_modules folders, Homebrew and Docker leave on your Mac.

Can Nadhif scan my website and server for vulnerabilities?

Yes. Nadhif tests websites you own with real attack techniques and scans Debian and Ubuntu servers for vulnerabilities over SSH.

Where can I get Nadhif?

On the official website, nadhif.hamou.de.
